newsitem.title: CHINA: China to punish stock market manipulators.
newsitem.headline: China to punish stock market manipulators.

text.p: China's top securities watchdog said there had been excessive speculation and manipulation in the stock market and threatened severe punishment if anyone was found guilty of it, Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.

In an urgent notice, the China Securities Regulatory Commission claimed a clutch of individuals and institutions had recently spread rumours in the market and "furiously stir-fried" selected shares to manipulate the market.
"This has greatly affected the healthy development of the securities market," the notice said.

The CSRC said it would "severely deal" with market manipulators. Those institutions found of creating and spreading false information would have their licences revoked and would be prosecuted, it said.
The CSRC said that market manipulation included:
-- institutions collaborating to concentrate their money on certain stocks to control prices.
-- institutions trying to spread rumours and false information to influence issues and trading of securities.
-- anyone continuously trading a certain number of stocks with the aim of distorting prices in either direction.
-- listed firms buying their own shares themselves or collaborating with others to buy them.
The CSRC also banned institutions from opening accounts in the name of individuals.
It urged exchanges to strengthen supervision of extraordinary stock price movements, investigate suspected manipulators and report them to the CSRC.

Local securities authorities must strengthen checks on information vendors to find those that spread rumours and false information with the aim of manipulating the market and must severely punish the manipulators, the CSRC notice said.
